A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same 3DGraphLLM work. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching retained material across substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark results, ablations, inference measurements, and qualitative examples for 3DGraphLLM.

after.justification: v3 reports original benchmark results and expanded ablations, runtime measurements, scalability results, and qualitative analyses.

M1.justification: The proposed encoders, projection modules, object identifiers, semantic-relation triplets, nearest-neighbor filters, loss, and two-stage training procedure are retained. The more explicit treatment of 2D features and NMS describes components already present in v1; expanded training data and new ablation variants do not establish a changed core method.

E1.justification: v3 adds 3RQA question-answering data and Nr3D-derived caption training, and uses RioRefer queries as caption targets, substantially expanding training coverage across task-data combinations. The five main ScanNet benchmarks remain. v1's RioRefer grounding evaluations disappear, although RioRefer remains a training source.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds LEO, Robin3D, GPT4Scene-HD, and GPT4Scene-HDM while retaining the earlier comparator set. v3 also introduces a direct token-count and latency comparison with GPT4Scene in Table 3, substantially updating the competitive evaluation.

E3.justification: The reported learning rate changes from 2e-5 to 5e-6. More substantially, segmentation ablations move from v1's frozen-LLM, projection-only setup without added object tokens to v3's full training pipeline with GT pretraining. New protocols compare pretraining corpora and triplet representations, and measure scalability at 10, 50, and 100 objects.

E4.justification: v3 adds direct triplet-versus-edge-sequence ablations, pretraining-corpus comparisons, neighbor-count studies for captioning and question answering, and object-count scalability analysis. It expands segmentation analyses across tasks and adds a caption-metric failure example. Conversely, v1's embedding PCA analysis and spatial-relation-module ablation are removed; the original functional-query and spatial-failure examples remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the experiments. The additional results retain the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces the LLAMA3 results: ScanRefer Acc@0.5 changes from 54.6 to 56.6, Multi3DRefer F1@0.5 from 58.2 to 59.9, and Scan2Cap CIDEr@0.5 from 82.9 to 81.0. These accompany revised training and are not controlled same-setting gains. Numerous new ablation, qualitative, latency, and memory results further expand the reported findings.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 corrects the sparse-graph token count from n + 3nk to 2n + 3nk, accounting for both identifier and 2D-feature tokens and matching the retained 800-token example. The loss and other formal definitions remain essentially unchanged; no theoretical propositions or proofs are added.

C1.justification: The central contribution remains a learnable semantic scene-graph representation for LLMs. Headline empirical claims shift from state-of-the-art grounding and captioning to grounding leadership and improvements over Chat-Scene across five benchmarks. v3 additionally claims up to fivefold faster inference than LVLM methods.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantial discussion of reference-based captioning and QA metric limitations, including a reportedly correct caption receiving zero CIDEr. It explains task-dependent neighbor-count behavior and interprets object-count scaling as practically manageable. Under revised experiments, it favors Mask3D where v1 reported little difference between segmenters; the original resource and segmentation limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 revises the hardware/time report from one A100 and approximately 72 hours to four A100s and approximately 24 hours. It newly specifies 370K instruction examples, a OneFormer3D confidence cutoff of 0.1, and conversion of referring expressions into caption targets. Most architectural and training details, and the public-code link, are retained.

R1.justification: References add ReferIt3D, LEO, Robin3D, and GPT4Scene, while the original Chat-3D reference associated with the former ablation setup is removed. New discussion positions the work against recent methods through inference cost and training-data scale, but the broader literature framing and central novelty position remain.

P1.justification: v3 rewrites the abstract and substantial introductory prose, reorders related-work themes, consolidates the two earlier ablation sections into Section 4.2, and reorganizes the appendices. These constitute substantial language and narrative restructuring beyond the added experimental content.

P2.justification: The document changes from predominantly single-column to two-column presentation. The architecture diagram is redrawn horizontally, Table 2 gains feature and LLM columns, and qualitative illustrations are recomposed. New tables and multi-task plots are added, while the PCA display is removed and retained appendix examples are redesigned.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens empirical support through segmentation ablations using the full training pipeline, a direct triplet-encoding comparison, newer baselines, and scalability evidence. These benefits are tempered by removal of the PCA and spatial-module checks and a new reporting inconsistency: the text claims improved Vicuna captioning with pretraining, while Table 4 shows CIDEr falling from 80.4 to 79.2 and BLEU-4 also declining. The stronger validation supports a limited net quality improvement.
